calls.title: Strong discovery-led call, no pricing objection

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: Thanks for making the time, Marcus. I want to keep this to fifteen minutes: understand how you review calls at UFC Elite today, and if it's a fit, agree a next step. Sound fair?

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: That works. We've got a lot on, so let's be efficient.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: Before we dive in, we work with twelve combat-sports gyms on exactly this, so I've seen how messy call reviews get at your scale.

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: Alright, I'm listening.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: How do you review sales calls with your membership team at the moment?

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: Honestly, we don't really. My managers listen to a few calls when they can, but it's ad hoc.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: And when a rep loses a deal, how do you know why?

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: We mostly don't. We see the number at the end of the month and guess.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: If you brought in something like this, who would need to sign it off?

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: That'd be me and my operations partner, Dana. She controls the budget.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: That's really helpful. Given the ad hoc reviews and the guesswork on lost deals, would it make sense to get you and Dana on a short demo next Tuesday?

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: Tuesday works. Send the invite for 2pm.

calls.title: Timing and authority stall handled poorly

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: Hi Priya, thanks for hopping on. I'll walk you through what we do and see if it's useful.

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: Sure, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: So we're an AI sales trainer that scores calls and coaches reps.

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: Okay. We're pretty busy right now though.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: How are you handling coaching today?

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: We do a bit here and there, nothing formal.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: Got it. So this could really help.

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: Maybe. I'd need to speak with my partner before anything, and honestly I need to think about it.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: Of course, totally understand. No pressure at all.

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: Yeah, let me chew on it.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: Sounds good, I'll follow up sometime next week.

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: Fine.

expected_criteria.label: Set agenda and establish credibility

evidence.quote: I'll walk you through what we do and see if it's useful.
evidence.speaker: rep

expected_criteria.why_points_lost: Opened with a loose purpose but set no time-boxed agenda and gave no credibility anchor before launching into the pitch.
expected_criteria.coaching_action: Open with a structured agenda and a proof point relevant to the buyer's world before pitching.

expected_criteria.label: Uncover pain, current process and decision route

evidence.quote: We do a bit here and there, nothing formal.
evidence.speaker: buyer

expected_criteria.why_points_lost: Uncovered only that coaching is informal; never quantified the cost of that gap and never identified who signs off, so the decision route stayed unknown.
expected_criteria.coaching_action: Ask for the cost of the current gap and the decision route before moving toward a pitch.

expected_criteria.label: Isolate price concern and reframe value

evidence.quote: I'd need to speak with my partner before anything, and honestly I need to think about it.
evidence.speaker: buyer

evidence.quote: Of course, totally understand. No pressure at all.
evidence.speaker: rep

expected_criteria.why_points_lost: Accepted the 'speak with my partner' authority stall and the 'need to think about it' timing stall with no diagnosis of the real blocker and no attempt to isolate or reframe the concern.
expected_criteria.coaching_action: Turn a vague stall into a named decision blocker and offer to include the partner rather than accepting the delay.

expected_criteria.label: Secure clear next step and commitment

evidence.quote: Sounds good, I'll follow up sometime next week.
evidence.speaker: rep

expected_criteria.why_points_lost: Closed with 'I'll follow up sometime next week' — no date, no owner and no commitment from the buyer.
expected_criteria.coaching_action: Lock a specific dated next step with the named decision maker before ending the call.

calls.title: Trust objection: buyer sceptical of AI coaching

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: Thanks Alex. Quick agenda: understand how you coach reps now, show how our AI review works, and see if a trial makes sense.

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: Okay, though I'll be honest, I'm sceptical about AI for this.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: Fair. We work with several gyms who felt the same, so I'll show you exactly how it scores, not a black box.

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: Go on.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: How do you coach your reps on calls today?

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: My head of sales listens back occasionally, but it's inconsistent.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: And the AI thing, what worries you?

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: I don't trust AI coaching. It doesn't get the nuance of a real sales conversation.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: That's fair. It doesn't replace your head of sales, it flags the moments to review and always shows the transcript quote behind every score, so a human makes the call.

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: Hmm. That's a bit more reassuring.

transcript.speaker: rep
transcript.text: Would you be open to a short pilot on ten real calls so you can judge the scores yourself?

transcript.speaker: buyer
transcript.text: Send me something and I'll consider a pilot.

expected_criteria.label: Set agenda and establish credibility

evidence.quote: Quick agenda: understand how you coach reps now, show how our AI review works, and see if a trial makes sense.
evidence.speaker: rep

evidence.quote: We work with several gyms who felt the same, so I'll show you exactly how it scores, not a black box.
evidence.speaker: rep

expected_criteria.coaching_action: Good: pre-empted the AI scepticism with a transparency-led credibility line.

expected_criteria.label: Uncover pain, current process and decision route

evidence.quote: My head of sales listens back occasionally, but it's inconsistent.
evidence.speaker: buyer

expected_criteria.why_points_lost: Got the current process but never quantified the cost of inconsistent coaching and never established who signs off, so the decision route was missed.
expected_criteria.coaching_action: Probe the cost of inconsistent coaching and confirm the decision maker before pitching.

expected_criteria.label: Isolate price concern and reframe value

evidence.quote: I don't trust AI coaching. It doesn't get the nuance of a real sales conversation.
evidence.speaker: buyer

evidence.quote: it flags the moments to review and always shows the transcript quote behind every score, so a human makes the call.
evidence.speaker: rep

expected_criteria.why_points_lost: Acknowledged the AI-trust concern and gave a good human-in-the-loop reassurance, but offered no concrete proof, reference or trial evidence, so the scepticism was softened rather than resolved.
expected_criteria.coaching_action: Back the reassurance with a proof point or reference, then confirm the concern is fully resolved before advancing.

expected_criteria.label: Secure clear next step and commitment

evidence.quote: Would you be open to a short pilot on ten real calls so you can judge the scores yourself?
evidence.speaker: rep

evidence.quote: Send me something and I'll consider a pilot.
evidence.speaker: buyer

expected_criteria.why_points_lost: Proposed a concrete pilot but did not lock a date or a named decision, leaving it at 'I'll consider a pilot'.
expected_criteria.coaching_action: Attach a date and an owner to the pilot before ending the call.

expected_objection_matches.detected_text: I don't trust AI coaching. It doesn't get the nuance of a real sales conversation.

evidence.quote: I don't trust AI coaching. It doesn't get the nuance of a real sales conversation.
evidence.speaker: buyer

calls.expected_summary: Trust objection well pre-empted and partly addressed with a human-in-the-loop framing, but no proof point closed it out; discovery skipped cost and decision route, and the pilot was proposed without a date. A mixed call with clear next-step and proof-point coaching.
